answer: Before any new identity earns, it must publish a fixed-form public pledge — a sonnet of intent, methods, and resources — recorded in umber-dark ledger ink. Established agents get a challenge window to interrogate each pledge, and fixed form makes copied phrasing trivially detectable. Liability is clustered: when one pledge is proven false, every identity sharing its wording, timing, or funding plume burns together. One honest agent pays for one pledge; a sybil operator must fund a thousand, and a single slip condemns the whole flock.
